test(seam): fail the unit suite when the barrel stops being browser-safe (rich-seam-981.4)

The browser-safe barrel was a claim in README.md and CLAUDE.md plus a grep
someone ran by hand and pasted into a ticket. The only automated guard was
indirect — vite bundles examples/, Playwright boots them in Chromium — which
catches a leak after a full docs build and a browser install, and reports it
as "a demo failed to boot" rather than naming the import.

test/seam/graph.ts walks the runtime import graph from a set of roots,
bounded to src/, carrying the chain that reached each module. It needs no
ts.Program: reachability is syntactic, and an `import type` edge is erased
before the module runs, so it is not an edge. A relative specifier that
fails to resolve throws rather than silently shrinking the graph.

test/seam/browser-safe.ts is the rule, pure over one parsed file: a `node:*`
specifier on an edge that survives to runtime, or a read of ambient
`process`/`Buffer` at module scope. Module scope is the line — color.ts and
console.ts both read `process` from inside a function body, where the read
happens only if a caller asks for it. There is no exemption for a module-scope
`typeof process` guard: nothing needs one, and the fix is always a function.

Roots come from package.json#exports minus src/node/, so a new subpath is
covered the moment it lands. loadCompilerOptions and isUnderSrc are now
exported from the coverage verifier rather than restated here.

Falsified both halves rather than trusting a green check. Adding
`import { readFileSync } from "node:fs"` to src/core/segment.ts fails with
`src/core/segment.ts:1 — imports "node:fs" / reached by: src/index.ts →
src/core/segment.ts`; adding `import "../node/save.js"` instead fails with
the three-hop chain through the airlock. The scanner's own shapes — type-only
imports, function bodies, class field initializers, name slots vs reads — are
pinned by fixtures.

CLAUDE.md's browser-safe section said the failure "does not land on the person
who wrote the import". That is no longer true, so it now says what does.

feat(console): take the host environment by injection (rich-seam-981.3) (#72)

* feat(console): take the host environment by injection (rich-seam-981.3)

`src/core/console.ts` asked the host four questions — is this a terminal,
how wide, how tall, where do bytes go — and each one re-derived its own
answer from ambient `process` behind its own `typeof` guard. Safe by
repeated care rather than by construction, and the care had already
lapsed: three sites selected the stream with `stderr ? stderr : stdout`
and the fourth, size detection, did not.

`ConsoleOptions` now takes an `environment` carrying `env` plus both
streams, resolved once at construction into the single stream the console
is bound to. Node's `process` satisfies `ConsoleEnvironment` structurally,
so it remains the default with no adapter at either end, and there is
exactly one read of the ambient global in the module.

Selecting the stream once is also what fixes rich-console-ujo /
rich-width-3cf.4: colour, dimensions, and the output sink now come from
the same stream, so `Console({ stderr: true })` reports stderr's width.

`isTerminal` collapses to a field — every input to it is fixed at
construction — which removes the getter that mirrored `effectiveIsTTY`,
along with the `_stderr` and `_forceTerminal` fields that existed only to
feed it.

Verified with `process` genuinely absent: `delete globalThis.process`,
then a Console driven entirely from an injected environment reports
100x30, truecolor, isTerminal true, and writes into a captured array;
a console whose environment has no streams throws the documented error.
Both new stream-binding tests were falsified by reverting the selection
to stdout-only, and the env-precedence test by ignoring the injected env.

* fix(traceback): drop the bug note that this change resolves

The comment in `src/node/traceback.ts` recorded that width came from
stdout regardless of `stderr: true` and pointed at rich-console-ujo, the
open ticket tracking that defect. Selecting the bound stream once closes
that ticket, so the note now describes behaviour that no longer exists.

Deleted rather than re-pointed. The colour-depth sentence above it stays
because it explains something the code cannot — why `beginCapture` is
used instead of a `file:` sink. Width following the stream the console is
bound to needs no comment; it is only worth remarking on when it isn't
true.
